title: Keep guessable formats out of scoring
statement: Keep true/false and other two-option items out of scored decisions, and score a multi-select item only when its stem says how many to choose and its scoring rule is declared.
example: In one course, 4 of 48 multi-select stems did not announce how to select.
detail: An assessment BrainLift in the reading course's feedback bans true/false from summative pools, and any multi-select without a principled scoring rule, because these formats are unusually sensitive to guessing, cueing and ambiguous category boundaries; one review round's feedback added that a two-option yes/no is a 50/50 guess. The course's assessment memo then counted 0 of 432 items as true/false, declared all-or-nothing scoring for multi-select, and found 44 of 48 multi-select stems announcing how to select and 4 not; its quality standard requires an explicit count in multi-select stems.
against: A multiple-choice BrainLift in the same file holds that single true/false items are nearly useless for inference but that in bundles of 15 or more the guessing averages out and the format becomes more defensible (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/feedback/feedback3/WF - Assessment  Feedback Brain - 260624-200115.md`, line 2008).
